title: What is the value of each division?
description: Ten divisions of whole numbers, fractions and mixed numbers are worked out by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor. The first answer is checked by multiplying back.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, and common factors are divided out first. Watch for students who turn the dividend upside down instead of the divisor.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions), Q1
video_script.why: The child uses the multiply by the reciprocal method of the solved example on ten divisions.
video_script.substitution: the book's own ten divisions, from three divided by seven ninths to a mixed number divided by a mixed number
video_script.anchor: a list of ten divisions, each with its divisor circled
video_script.payoff_line: The last answer is eight thirds, which is two and two thirds
video_script.fraction_reading: seven ninths, nine sevenths, fourteen quarters, sixteen ninths, forty nine quarters, nine fifths, two elevenths, eight thirds
video_script.design: A list of ten divisions. Each line shows the divisor turned upside down, then the product with common factors divided out. The last line shows the check.
open_questions: Ten divisions are grouped into five steps of two lines each and one check, so the board stays short.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a list of ten divisions of fractions, whole numbers and mixed numbers

marks.list: the ten divisions arrive in a list
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the list

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing fractions.
<bookmark mark='list'/>It has ten divisions, such as three divided by seven ninths, and fourteen quarters divided by two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the value of each division?

beats.on_screen: the list stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a fraction and the same fraction turned upside down, joined by a curved arrow; the word reciprocal appears

marks.rule: the divisor is circled and the sign changes from divide to times
marks.name: the upside down fraction is labelled reciprocal

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A fraction turned upside down is called its reciprocal.

beats.on_screen: Given: ten divisions of whole numbers, fractions and mixed numbers

marks.given: the ten divisions are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, ten divisions of whole numbers, fractions and mixed numbers.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each division

marks.find: the words To find and the question are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the value of each division.

marks.one: the first division is rewritten with the reciprocal of its divisor
marks.two: the second division is rewritten with one half

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, three divided by seven ninths is three times nine sevenths, which is twenty seven sevenths.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Fourteen quarters divided by two is fourteen quarters times one half, which is seven quarters.

marks.three: the third division is rewritten with its reciprocal
marks.four: the fourth division is shortened and then multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, two thirds times three halves is six over six, which is one.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Fourteen sixths times three sevenths shortens to two over two, which is one.

marks.five: the fifth division is rewritten with its reciprocal
marks.six: the sixth division is rewritten with seven

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, four thirds times four thirds is sixteen ninths.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Seven quarters times seven is forty nine quarters.

marks.seven: eight halves is written as four, then multiplied by fifteen quarters
marks.eight: the eighth division is rewritten with nine

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step four, eight halves is four, and four times fifteen quarters shortens to fifteen.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>One fifth times nine is nine fifths.

marks.nine: six and twelve are linked by a line and divided by six
marks.mixed: both mixed numbers are written as fractions
marks.ten: the two elevens are linked by a line and divided by eleven

beats.colours: the shared factors in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step five, one sixth times twelve elevenths shortens to two over eleven, which is two elevenths.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>Three and two thirds is eleven thirds, and one and three eighths is eleven eighths.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Eleven thirds times eight elevenths has eleven on top and below, so both are shortened.

marks.back: the answer is multiplied by the divisor
marks.match: the result is matched with the first number in the division

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step six, check the first answer.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Twenty seven sevenths times seven ninths shortens to three, the number we started with.

marks.ans: the ten answers are boxed in order
marks.mid: the next answers are read along the box
marks.last: the last answer is written as a mixed number beside the box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first four answers are twenty seven sevenths, seven quarters, one and one.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Then come sixteen ninths, forty nine quarters, fifteen, nine fifths and two elevenths.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last answer is eight thirds, which is two and two thirds.
